subject.title: Feature Request: Batch API support for background tasks

question: Should provider Batch API turns become a first-class asynchronous task type, and should the initial supported caller be isolated cron only or every background entry point?
rationale: Current task infrastructure can own persistence, but the provider lifecycle and agent-loop semantics remain immediate and stream-oriented; choosing the permanent contract, fallback behavior, and initial scope requires maintainer product and API intent.

options.title: Start with isolated cron
options.body: Define a generic delayed provider-turn contract backed by tasks, prove it for isolated cron agentTurn jobs, then evaluate subagents and heartbeat separately.

options.title: Design every entry point
options.body: Specify cron, sessions_send, sessions_spawn, subagents, and heartbeat together before implementation, accepting a substantially broader initial program.

options.title: Decline full-agent batching
options.body: Keep provider Batch APIs outside the OpenClaw agent loop and support only external pure-prompt batch workflows.

recommendation.title: Start with isolated cron
recommendation.body: Define a generic delayed provider-turn contract backed by tasks, prove it for isolated cron agentTurn jobs, then evaluate subagents and heartbeat separately.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged history covers the provider plugin boundary, subagent invocation, and heartbeat runtime affected by the decision.
